test_title: PYST 33 - SSC CHSL 2025 - English Language (Held On: 25 Nov, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: english
question:
Choose the correct indirect narration of the following statement from the given alternatives:

The judge said, "What do you have to say on your defence?"

options.text: The judge asked what he was to say on his defence.
The judge asked what he will have to say on his defence.
The judge asked what he is to say on his defence.
The judge asked what he had to say on his defence.

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indirect Speech:** The judge asked what he had to say on his defence.
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **Direct to Indirect Speech:**
 
 
• The reporting verb "said" is changed to "asked" because the original sentence is a question.
 
• The question format changes to a statement format in indirect speech.
 
 
 
• **Tense Change:**
 
 
• The verb "do" in the direct speech is changed to "had" in the indirect speech as the reporting verb is in the past tense.
 
• This follows the rule of sequence of tenses.
 
 
 
• **Pronoun Change:**
 
 
• The pronoun "you" is changed to "he" to match the subject of the reporting clause.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Punctuation and Format:**
 
 
• In indirect speech, quotation marks are removed.
 
• The sentence is written as a statement rather than a question.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *The judge asked what he had to say on his defence.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** The judge asked what he was to say on his defence. 
 
 
• Incorrect as "was to say" implies a planned or future action, which does not fit the context.
 
 
 
• **Option 2:** The judge asked what he will have to say on his defence.
 
 
• Incorrect as "will have to say" uses future tense, which is not appropriate when the reporting verb is in the past tense.
 
 
 
• **Option 3:** The judge asked what he is to say on his defence. 
 
 
• Incorrect as "is to say" uses present tense, which does not align with the past reporting verb.
